messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: dedicated-cluster-latency — tenant=acme-corp, alert_id=PD-87921. P95 latency spiked to 28s, error rate 12% (5xx). Page routed to eng-oncall rotation.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-87921 — triggered, auto-escalation in 5m if not acknowledged.

sara: acked. I'm on it. Paging primary oncall for dedicated clusters.

mike: grabbing logs + metrics now. seeing increased queue depth on acme-corp pool GPUs and many "failed to allocate KV cache" errors.

jess: joining. starting a quick call — link: https://call.example/redwood/PD-87921

alejandro: I can take the infra side if we need to add capacity. Noted the reserved capacity autoscaler for this tenant showed "scale blocked: capacity" earlier.

mike: here's the short grep from runtime logs (tail):
```
2026-02-21T03:12:04Z runtime: tenant=acme-corp request_id=3f9a P95_latency=28.4s error=internal_server_error msg="nvml: out of memory?"
2026-02-21T03:12:07Z runtime: tenant=acme-corp kv_cache_alloc_failed count=42
2026-02-21T03:12:12Z scheduler: node=dedicated-pool-7 pod=acme-worker-2 status=CrashLoopBackOff
```

jess: Confirmed. Also seeing GPU queue length metric (gpu.request_queue) at 210 vs normal 5-15.

sara: Customer impact: AcmeCorp production traffic is affected. App team reports timeouts in their dashboards. We've already received one support ticket. Severity: P1.

alejandro: Running internal check for reserved nodes usage: `rbctl tenant show acme-corp --json` returns `reserved_replicas: 4, active_replicas: 2, pending: 0`. Looks like reserved capacity exists but not attached to pods. Possibly scheduler stuck.

mike: Running `kubectl get pods -n tenant-acme-corp` shows multiple pods in Pending/CrashLoop. Attaching snippet:
```
NAME                       READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
acme-worker-0              1/1     Running            0          12h
acme-worker-1              0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          2h
acme-worker-2              0/1     Pending            0          5m
```

jess: Could be node kubelet failing to mount hugepages after recent kernel update last night. Any recent infra deploys?

infra-bot: Deploy: kernel-update-2026-02-21 completed on cluster-dedicated-3 at 02:45Z by release-bot.

alejandro: Yup that matches. I see kernel-update completed across several dedicated nodes in that cluster. I'm rolling a quick health check on kubelet.

sara: Mitigation options we discussed: 1) Failover tenant to shared-hosted pool (short-term), 2) Force attach reserved nodes (bypass scheduler), 3) Rollback kernel update on affected nodes. Prefer a quick mitigation to restore customer traffic.

mike: Can we try soft-failover first: route a subset (10%) of AcmeCorp traffic to shared pool while we fix dedicated pool? We have route override `routectl set-tenant-route acme-corp --percent 10 --target shared`.

jess: I'm for failover -> reduces blast radius. If shared can handle their QPS. Check quota on shared.

alejandro: Shared pool headroom: p95 latency baseline 90ms, capacity ~40% free. Should be safe for a partial shift.

sara: Mike, please execute the 10% redirect. Alejandro, start rolling back kernel on the two newest nodes in cluster-dedicated-3. Jess, coordinate with support to inform AcmeCorp of partial failover.

mike: running: `routectl set-tenant-route acme-corp --percent 10 --target shared`

mike: command accepted. Wait a few mins for edge to adjust.

(2m)

mike: Edge reports 9.6% of requests now going to shared. p95 for tenant on shared is 180ms, error rate dropped to 4% overall, dedicated still painful but load slightly reduced.

alejandro: Starting rollback on nodes node-7 and node-9. `infractl rollback-kernel node-7 node-9 --version=2026-02-15`

infra-bot: Action queued: rollback-kernel for node-7,node-9. Estimated disruption: 90s per node (reboot).

jess: Noted. Can we choose nodes that have fewer pods first (node-9 appears low-util)?

alejandro: Yep picking node-9 first. Draining node-9 now: `kubectl drain node-9 --ignore-daemonsets`

mike: After drain, acme-worker-2 moved to node-11 but node-11 doesn't have GPU reserved for tenant -> went Pending. Hmm. We need to force attach reserved nodes as part of remediation.

alejandro: Running force-attach: `rbctl tenant attach-reserved --tenant acme-corp --nodes node-9,node-7` — that should bind the reserved GPU labels so pods can schedule.

infra-bot: rbctl: attaching reserved nodes node-9,node-7 to tenant acme-corp — success.

(5m)

mike: Pods coming up. acme-worker-2 moved to node-9 and shows Running. P95 for tenant down to 1.2s overall. Error rate falling to 1.8%.

sara: Good. Keep the 10% shared failover for another 10m to ensure stability, then ramp down. Jess send a short note to Acme support: we performed partial failover and are restoring dedicated cluster; will follow up with RCA.

jess: Message posted to AcmeCorp support channel and Cc'd account manager.

alejandro: node-9 rollback complete. node-7 scheduled next. I'll monitor kubelet logs for mounting errors.

mike: Observed root cause indicators: after kernel-update, kubelet reported "failed to reserve hugepages" and GPU driver NVML started returning intermittent allocation errors. Combined with scheduler bug in reserved attach, pods couldn't be scheduled even though reserved_replicas existed.

sara: Summary for incident record: - Trigger: P95 latency and 5xx spike for tenant acme-corp. - Impact: Partial production outage affecting customer requests (P1). - Cause (initial): kernel update + kubelet/hugepages + scheduler reserved-attach bug. - Mitigation: 1) 10% traffic failover to shared pool, 2) forced attach of reserved nodes, 3) rollback kernel on affected nodes. - Status: Restored, p95 ~1200ms then trending down.

(hand-off)
sara: handing off to jess for monitoring and RCA follow-up. I'm going offline for 30m. Notes: PD remains open until RCA stub created. Leave the route at 10% until jess confirms stable.

jess: Ack. I'll monitor for 60m and then ramp the route back to 100% dedicated if stable. Creating incident ticket: INC-2026-02-21-ACME-PD87921.

pagerduty: PD-87921 acknowledged by sara, assigned to jess.

jess: created RCA draft in docs: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-02-21-ACME-PD87921 — will ping infra + runtime for postmortem.

alejandro: I'll open a bug to prevent reserved-attach regressions and add a post-deploy check for hugepages allocation.

sara: Closing notes: escalate to eng-platform if we see repeated failures across dedicated clusters. Good job team. :thumbsup:

jess: 60m monitor complete — metrics stable, route ramping back to 100% dedicated now. P95 at 180ms on dedicated after ramp. Marking incident RESOLVED, will include timeline in RCA.

incident-bot: Incident PD-87921 marked RESOLVED by jess at 2026-02-21T04:40:00Z.
